summary: Construct a hard-surface object as named shells, inserts, fasteners and mating interfaces whose visible boundaries explain assembly and service access.
objective: A viewer can isolate each serviceable part, trace what locates and retains it, and move an articulated part without exposing impossible gaps or fused neighbours.
applies_when: A manufactured prop, enclosure, machine or architectural fixture must read as an assembly rather than one decorated solid.
intent_signals: show how a cover is retained
select product parts after glTF export
example_prompts: Build a rugged instrument enclosure with a removable battery door, locating lip and visible fasteners.
Create an inspectable pump housing whose cover, gasket seat, shaft and bearing cap remain separate runtime parts.
negative_signals: Add random panel lines to a solid block
Model hidden fasteners with no inspection or silhouette value
not_for: Manufacturing tolerances, structural loads or certified service procedures.
Bevel width and custom-normal setup, which belong to the linked geometry contract.

principles: Begin with a part-and-interface diagram: which part carries load visually, which closes an opening, which locates another part, and which feature retains it. A seam earns geometry when it marks one of those relationships.

Keep a functional part separate when selection, removal, articulation, material assignment or replacement needs independent identity. Merge purely decorative marks when separation adds no runtime or construction meaning.
A fastening story needs both sides. A visible screw head without a boss, flange or receiving region reads as decoration; a removable cover with no clearance path or retainer reads as fused geometry.
implementation: Block primary shell, frame, removable covers, inserts and moving parts as named Blender objects. Establish mating planes and opening envelopes before adding seams, ribs, vents or fastener heads.

Give a removable panel an edge condition: overlap lip, rebate, flange or deliberate butt seam. Add only the retention cues visible at the intended camera, and include a plausible removal direction and hand/tool clearance when serviceability is part of the story.

Use separate cutter and detail collections in the editable `.blend`; keep modifier order and source construction editable. Export the approved evaluated meshes through `knowledge.blender-evaluated-mesh-handoff` and use the linked bevel/normal contract for edge treatment.

Assign a stable application key as a Blender custom property for every interactive part and export Custom Properties to glTF extras. Treat display names as labels; Three.js lookup, selection, variants and motion use the explicit key and declared parent hierarchy.
Create selection proxies or simple bounds for thin fasteners and recessed parts when precise ray hits would be unreliable. Keep proxies application-side or visibly excluded from production rendering.
Inspect assembled, isolated and one-step-disassembled states. Reset restores the same hierarchy, local transforms and visible mating relationships.
observable_checks: In a three-quarter view, every major seam terminates at a meaningful boundary and does not drift across a supposedly single part.
Isolating a cover reveals a matching opening, seat or flange on the body; hiding a fastener does not remove unrelated shell geometry.
Moving the declared removable or hinged part through its path clears neighbours and retains its pivot or removal axis.
After glTF load, every interactive application key resolves exactly once and selects the intended mesh or group; proximity alone creates no joint.

creative_affordances: Retainers may be screws, latches, clips, pins or concealed attachment; choose one that matches the object's visual language.
Let wear, paint breaks or material contrast emphasize handled service boundaries without inventing extra seams.
known_limits: Readable construction does not certify manufacturability, ingress protection, fastening strength or repair safety.
glTF extras are application metadata with no universal behavior; the runtime must define its keys.
Authored reusable guidance; no Blender export, Three.js runtime or assembly artifact was executed for this record.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5's glTF exporter can export custom properties from most objects when Include > Custom Properties is selected, storing them in the corresponding glTF extras field; extras have no defined namespace and require application-specific meaning.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 exporter metadata transport only; it does not guarantee unique identifiers or runtime selection behavior.
